title: Cells: Plant and Animal Cells
seo_title: Primary 5 Science: Cells Worksheets – Plant and Animal Cells (with Answers)
standard_text: Recognise that the cell is the basic unit of life. Identify the parts of plant and animal cells (cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, chloroplasts) and their functions, and compare plant and animal cells (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on cells: cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus and chloroplasts, plant and animal cells, and using a microscope. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The cell is the basic unit of life.
key_sub: Plant cells have a cell wall and may have chloroplasts.
body_html:
How to think about it

All living things are made of cells. The cell is the basic unit of life.

  • Cell membrane: controls what enters and leaves the cell.
  • Cytoplasm: jelly-like; most activities happen here.
  • Nucleus: controls the cell's activities; contains genetic material.
  • Cell wall (plant cells only): gives a regular shape and support.
  • Chloroplasts (plant cells in green parts): contain chlorophyll to make food.
Example

A cell has a cell wall but no chloroplasts. Is it a plant or an animal cell?

Only plant cells have a cell wall

It may be from a root or an onion

Answer: A plant cell.

Example

Why can we not see cells with our eyes?

Most cells are very small

We need a microscope

Answer: They are too small.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking animal cells have a cell wall. Only plant cells do.
  • Thinking all plant cells have chloroplasts. Root and onion cells do not.
  • Mixing up the cell wall and the cell membrane. The membrane controls movement in and out; the wall gives shape.
  • Starting with the high-power lens on a microscope. Start with low power.

faq.q: What is the difference between plant and animal cells?
faq.a: Plant cells have a cell wall and many have chloroplasts. Animal cells have neither. Both have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus.

faq.q: Do all plant cells have chloroplasts?
faq.a: No. Only cells in the green parts that get light, such as leaf cells. Root cells and onion cells do not have chloroplasts.
